documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for a routine checkup, first in two years (missed the 2023 visit; travel). No symptoms at all. Energy good, weight steady, no GI complaints, no jaundice ever since the episode at 24.

Hx reviewed with him:
- Injection drug use in the past, in remission. Confirms no IV drug use now.
- Hepatitis about ten years ago after a trip abroad, never treated, got completely better. Still doesn't know which kind.
- Has never received blood products.
Meds: none. NKDA.
FHx: father, alcohol use disorder; mother, hypertension. Unchanged.
Social: still consulting in international logistics, on the road abroad several times a year. Never smoker. 1 to 2 drinks a week. PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

ROS: 12-point negative.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, normal BP. NAD. Sclerae anicteric. TMs and pharynx normal. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge not palpable, no splenomegaly. Skin without rash or stigmata of liver disease. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Assessment/plan:
- Routine adult exam. CMP, CBC, lipids.
- Hepatitis B: adults are now screened once regardless of risk, and with his history it is worth knowing his status. Sending surface antigen, surface antibody and core antibody, with e antigen and e antibody.
- Flu vaccine today (missed it in the fall).
- History of injection drug use, remains in remission.
One year.

documents.title: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Austin, your routine labs (kidney, liver, blood counts, cholesterol) are all normal.

The hepatitis B tests show that you had hepatitis B at some point in the past and your body cleared it. The surface antigen is negative, which means there is no active or chronic infection. The core antibody is positive, which is the footprint of an old infection, and the surface antibody is positive, which means you are immune now. The e antigen is negative and e antibody positive, which fits with a cleared infection too.

This most likely explains the hepatitis you had at 24. Nothing needs treatment, you don't need the hepatitis B vaccine, and you can't pass it on.

documents.title: RE: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks for explaining. Just so I'm clear, this isn't something I need to tell people about or get checked on every year?

documents.title: RE: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Correct. It's a past infection that's gone, not a current one. No yearly testing, no precautions with partners or anyone else. If a blood bank or a doctor ever asks, "had hepatitis B in the past, resolved" is the accurate answer.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, lot in MAR. Feeling well, no fever, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past. 15 min observation unremarkable. Offered this season's COVID vaccine, he declined for now; will think about it. Physical scheduled 12/11.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Doing well. Travel schedule heavy again this year; feels healthy, no complaints. Got his flu shot here in October; still not interested in the COVID booster.

Remains in remission from injection drug use, no use of any kind. Social drinker, unchanged. Never smoker. PHQ-2 negative.

PMH reviewed: remote IVDU in remission; resolved hepatitis at 24, which last year's serology showed was hepatitis B, cleared and immune. No meds. NKDA. FHx unchanged.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals normal (flowsheet). Well-appearing. Anicteric. Neck: no LAD. CV: regular, no murmur. Resp: clear. Abd: soft, nontender, nondistended, no HSM. Ext: warm, no edema. Skin: no lesions of concern.

A/P: healthy 35 y/o. CMP and lipids. Nothing else due. Back in a year.
